---
title: "Live demos"
subtitle: "The same warp code as `wxy warp`, compiled to WebAssembly"
---

The demos are hosted from [wxylib/web](https://github.com/wxylib/web).
Every view is a fresh warp: GDAL's chunked warp, kernels and overview
choice, fetching only the COG tiles the view touches over HTTP range
requests.

- [A COG in any projection](https://wxylib.org/web/cog.html): drag to
  pan, scroll to zoom, change the target CRS. Deep links take `?url=` and
  `?crs=`.
- [Sentinel-2 on a web map](https://wxylib.org/web/s2.html): a STAC
  search of the map view, and the chosen scene's raw band COGs warped onto
  the map's own grid. Deep links take `?from=` and `?to=` dates.
- [BRAN2023 from its byte table](https://wxylib.org/web/bran.html): a
  year of daily ocean temperature read in place from netCDF on NCI
  THREDDS, chunk by chunk, from a table of offsets. Plain JavaScript, no
  wasm: the table needs no library. Deep links take `?at=lon,lat`.
- [An editing canvas with CAD control](https://wxylib.org/web/edit.html):
  draw and edit vector data exactly, with snapping, typed distance and
  angle locks, an undoable operation log, a nudge brush, edits in a
  chosen CRS with ground or grid measures, and a COG underlay warped into
  the same frame. Opens on a sample; takes GeoJSON by file, drop or
  `?url=`. The design is in
  [m18](design/docs/m18-editing-canvas.md).

```{=html}
<iframe class="demo" src="https://wxylib.org/web/" title="wxylib browser demos" loading="lazy"></iframe>
```
